context:
Goal: the phone's order stamps look and work like the web's.
Problem: step 6 ships two choices the mockup didn't have. The note field is two lines tall where the mockup shows one, so it fits the 44-point tap minimum at larger text sizes. And the "0 stamped" filter cell shows greyed out when nothing is stamped. Both depart from the mockup, so they need your word. Step 6 merges with them meanwhile.
Based on: the step 6 design review (read).
Based on: house rule ux-house-rules-govern: tap targets at least 44 points (ruling).
Departs from: the step 6 mockup's one-line note field and its always-active "0 stamped" cell.
Meanwhile: step 6 ships with both. A change later is a small edit.

options.gain: The note field is easy to tap, and the filter can't show an empty list.
options.how: Two-line note field; "0 stamped" greyed out when empty.
options.label: Keep both
options.lose: It differs a little from the mockup.

options.gain: It looks exactly like the mockup.
options.how: A one-line note field with a taller tap area; "0 stamped" always active.
options.label: Match the mockup
options.lose: More work. Tapping "0 stamped" can show an empty list.

title: The phone's stamp editor: a two-line note field and a greyed-out "0 stamped" cell. Keep both?
why: Both follow the house tap-size rule, and neither can show you a dead end.
